hindi: आदित्यों के लिए, राजाओं के लिए, पुरातन काल से घी टपकाने वाली इन स्तुतियों को मैं जुहू से अर्पित करता हूँ। मित्र, अर्यमा, भग, महान् जन्म वाला वरुण, दक्ष और अंश हमें सुनें।
english: These hymns dripping with ghee I offer with the ladle for the Ādityas, for the kings, from of old. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, the mighty-born Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa hear us.
notes: 'gira' + 'ā' (girāḥ ādityebhyaḥ) is read as acc. pl.; 'ghṛtasnūḥ' is taken with the hymns, though it could also qualify the ladle. 'tuvijātaḥ' may be an epithet of Varuṇa or of the whole list; it is placed with Varuṇa by position. The singular verb śṛṇotu serves the whole list.

hindi: एक संकल्प वाले मित्र, अर्यमा और वरुण आज मेरी इस स्तुति को स्वीकार करें; आदित्य, जो उज्ज्वल, धारा से पवित्र, निष्कपट, निर्दोष और अक्षत हैं।
english: May Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, of one will, enjoy this praise of mine today; the Ādityas, bright, purified by streams, without crookedness, faultless, unharmed.
notes: dhārapūtāḥ is read as 'purified by streams' (literal). The second line is a list in apposition and has no verb of its own.

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. des. √dabh

hindi: वे आदित्य, विशाल, गम्भीर, अप्रतारित, हानि की इच्छा करने वाले, बहुत आँखों वाले हैं। वे भीतर देखते हैं, टेढ़े को और सीधे को भी; राजाओं के लिए सब कुछ, दूर से दूर भी, समीप है।
english: They, the Ādityas, wide, deep, unbeguiled, wishing to harm, many-eyed. They see within the crooked and the straight; for the kings everything, even the farthest things, is near.
notes: dipsantaḥ is unclear: literally 'wishing to harm/deceive'; whom they wish to harm is not stated, so the participle is left as it stands. The words 'antaḥ paśyanti' could also be read 'see within'.

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. √rakṣ
m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. √ci

hindi: आदित्य देवों ने चलने वाले और स्थिर को धारण किया, जो सारे भुवन के रक्षक हैं; दीर्घ विचार वाले, प्रभुत्व की रक्षा करते हुए, सत्य के पालक, ऋणों पर ध्यान रखते हुए।
english: The Ādityas upheld what moves and what stands, the gods, guardians of the whole world; of far-reaching thought, guarding lordship, keepers of truth, taking note of debts.
notes: dhārayanta is read as 3 pl. impf. mid.; the sense of cayamānāḥ with ṛṇāni ('taking note of debts') is uncertain (√ci can mean requite or heed). 'jagat sthāḥ' read as the moving and the standing.

hindi: हे आदित्यो, हम तुम्हारी इस सहायता को पाएँ, जो हे अर्यमा, भय में भी सुख देने वाली है। हे मित्र और वरुण, तुम्हारे मार्गदर्शन में मैं गड्ढों की तरह बुराइयों से बचूँ।
english: May we find, O Ādityas, this help of yours, which, O Aryaman, brings comfort even in fear. In your guidance, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I avoid evils as one avoids pits.
notes: 'bhaya ā cit' is read as bhaye + ā cit; 'ā' here is taken as emphatic. 'śvabhreva' read as śvabhrā iva; 'as one avoids' is the natural sense of the comparison.

hindi: हे अर्यमा, हे मित्र, तुम्हारा मार्ग सुगम है, काँटों से रहित है; हे वरुण, वह सीधा है। हे आदित्यो, उससे हमारे पक्ष में बोलो और हमें ऐसा आश्रय दो जिसे रोका न जा सके।
english: For your path, O Aryaman, O Mitra, is easy to go and free of thorns; O Varuṇa, it is straight. By that, O Ādityas, speak on our behalf, and give us shelter hard to ward off.
notes: 'duṣparihantu' is read as 'hard to ward off (strike away)'; 'adhi vocata' as 'speak on behalf of'.

hindi: अदिति, राजपुत्र और अर्यमा हमें सुगम मार्गों से शत्रुताओं के पार ले जाएँ। मित्र और वरुण के महान् आश्रय के समीप हम बहुत वीरों से युक्त और अक्षत रहें।
english: May Aditi, the sons of kings, and Aryaman carry us over hatreds by easy paths. May we be near the great shelter of Mitra and Varuṇa, rich in many heroes, unharmed.
notes: The singular verb pipartu serves Aditi, the sons of kings and Aryaman together. 'Sons of kings' is the literal phrase; the text does not name them in the line.

hindi: उन्होंने तीन भूमियों को और तीन द्युलोकों को धारण किया; इनके बीच यज्ञ में तीन व्रत हैं। हे आदित्यो, सत्य से तुम्हारी महिमा महान् है; हे अर्यमा, वरुण और मित्र, वह सुन्दर है।
english: They upheld the three earths and the three heavens; among these there are three ordinances in the rite. By truth, O Ādityas, great is your greatness; that, O Aryaman, Varuṇa and Mitra, is lovely.
notes: dhārayan is read as 3 pl. impf.; the subject is the Ādityas of the preceding verses. 'antar eṣām' is read 'among these'.

hindi: तीन दिव्य प्रकाशमान लोकों को उन्होंने धारण किया, सुनहरे, उज्ज्वल, धारा से पवित्र; न सोने वाले, पलक न झपकने वाले, अप्रतारित, विस्तृत यश वाले, सरल मनुष्य के लिए।
english: They upheld the three heavenly luminous realms, golden, bright, purified by streams; unsleeping, unwinking, unbeguiled, of wide renown, for the upright mortal.
notes: 'uruśaṃsāḥ' read as 'of wide renown' (alternatively 'widely ruling'); 'for the upright mortal' is loosely attached to the list.

hindi: हे वरुण, तुम सबके राजा हो, उनके भी जो देव हैं, हे असुर, और उनके भी जो मनुष्य हैं। हमें देखने के लिए सौ शरद ऋतुएँ दो; हम भली प्रकार स्थापित पूर्व आयु को प्राप्त करें।
english: You, O Varuṇa, are king of all, of those who are gods, O lord, and of those who are mortals. Give us a hundred autumns to see; may we reach the well placed former lifetimes.
notes: 'asura' in the vocative is rendered 'O lord' per the glossary. 'āyūṃṣi sudhitāni pūrvā' is read literally as 'well placed former lifetimes'; its exact sense is uncertain.

hindi: न दाहिना जाना जाता है, न बायाँ, न पूर्व, हे आदित्यो, और न पश्चिम। चाहे भोलेपन से, हे वसुओ, चाहे विचारशीलता से, तुमसे ले जाया गया मैं निर्भय प्रकाश को प्राप्त करूँ।
english: Neither the right is discerned, nor the left, nor the east, O Ādityas, nor the west. Whether through simplicity, O Vasus, or through thoughtfulness, led by you may I reach fearless light.
notes: Line a is read as a statement that directions are not discerned; the subject of cikite is only the directions. Line b: pākyā and dhīryā are read as instrumentals ('through simplicity', 'through thoughtfulness'); both are uncertain, and 'Vasus' is used as an address to the Ādityas.

hindi: जिसने सत्य से बंधे राजाओं को दान दिया, जिसे स्थायी पोषण बढ़ाते हैं, वह धनी रथ से सबसे आगे जाता है, वसुओं का दाता, यज्ञों में प्रशंसित।
english: He who has given to the truth-bound kings, whom lasting nourishments strengthen, that wealthy one goes first by chariot, a giver of goods, praised at the rites.
notes: ṛtanibhyaḥ is unclear (read as 'truth-bound'); 'vasudāvā' read as 'giver of goods'. 'Vasus' is not meant here, only vasu 'goods'.

hindi: पवित्र, अप्रतारित, वह जलों और उत्तम चरागाहों के पास रहता है, पूर्ण आयु वाला, उत्तम वीरों से युक्त। जो आदित्यों के मार्गदर्शन में है, उसे न समीप से, न दूर से कोई मारता है।
english: Pure, unbeguiled, he dwells near the waters and good pastures, of full vigour, rich in heroes. No one strikes him, from near or from afar, who is in the guidance of the Ādityas.
notes: 'śucir apaḥ' is read as śuciḥ apaḥ with apaḥ as accusative plural 'waters'; the alternative reading 'pure worker' is possible. vṛddhavayāḥ is read 'of full vigour'.

hindi: हे अदिति, हे मित्र और वरुण, कृपा करो, जो कोई अपराध हमने तुम्हारे प्रति किया हो। हे इन्द्र, मैं विस्तृत निर्भय प्रकाश को प्राप्त करूँ; लम्बे अन्धकार हम तक न पहुँचें।
english: O Aditi, O Mitra and Varuṇa, be gracious, whatever offence we have committed against you. May I reach the wide fearless light, O Indra; may the long darknesses not reach us.
notes: The mix of addressees (Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, then Indra) is as printed; 'yat vaḥ' is read as 'whatever, against you'.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. ā-√ji

hindi: दोनों मिलकर उसके लिए आकाश की वर्षा को बढ़ाते हैं; वह भाग्यवान्, पुष्ट होता हुआ। दोनों निवासों को जीतता हुआ वह युद्धों में जाता है; दोनों वर्धक उसके लिए अच्छे होते हैं।
english: Both, joined together, swell for him the rain of heaven, the fortunate one, thriving. Winning both dwellings he goes in battles; both increasers become good for him.
notes: The two 'both' (ubhe, ubhā) are not identified in the verse. 'nāma' read as 'indeed'; it may mean 'by name' (named Fortunate). 'pṛtsūbhāvardhaṷ' read as pṛtsu ubhā vardhau; the printed 'ṷ' mark is a scan artefact for u. The reading of ājayan is also uncertain.

hindi: हे पूजनीय आदित्यो, तुम्हारी जो मायाएँ हैं, जो हानि करने वाले, शत्रु के लिए फैलाए हुए फंदे हैं। घोड़ों वाले की तरह मैं रथ से उनके पार जाऊँ; अक्षत हम विस्तृत आश्रय में रहें।
english: O worshipful Ādityas, your wiles which are snares spread out for the harmful one, for the deceiver. Like one with horses, may I go beyond them by chariot; unharmed, may we be in the wide shelter.
notes: Line a has no finite verb; 'pāśāḥ ... vicṛttāḥ' is read in apposition to māyāḥ. Line b: 'ati yeṣam' read as 1 sg. optative of √i (alternative: yeṣām genitive), and 'urāvā' as urau ā; both uncertain.

hindi: हे वरुण, मैं उदार, प्रिय और बहुत देने वाले मित्र की ओर से रिक्तता को न पाऊँ। हे राजन्, मैं सुसंयत धन से नीचे न गिरूँ; उत्तम वीरों से युक्त हम यज्ञ में ऊँचे स्वर में बोलें।
english: O Varuṇa, may I not come upon emptiness from a bounteous, dear, much-giving friend. O king, may I not fall away from well held wealth; rich in heroes, may we speak greatly at the rite.
notes: The syntax of line a ('ā vidam śūnam āpeḥ') is uncertain: āpeḥ is read as a genitive of the friend and the whole as 'emptiness from the friend'. 'ava sthām' is read as 'may I not fall away' (alternative: 'stand away from').
